Note: `_escapeMention` escapes `&`, `<`, `>` but not quotes — that's fine for text. `_macroParamText` compares `_attrOf(open, 'ac:name') == paramName` — case sensitivity? Java Jsoup parameter() — probably exact. Hmm.

Potential issues to note:
1. `_findPage` cache stores null results too (good, caches misses). But cache is per inliner instance.
2. `_includeTarget`: `title!` — `_nonBlank(title) ? title : _macroParamText(...)`. If title from ri:content-title is blank and page-title param is used... fine. But there's a subtle bug: if the `ri:content-title` attribute is present but blank (e.g. `ri:content-title=""`), title falls to param. OK.
3. In `_resolveInclude`, `_storageValueOf(page)` is called before null check — page is `Map<String,dynamic>?`, `_storageValueOf` accepts nullable. Fine.
4. `_macroNameOf(macro)!` non-null asserted — the include macro pattern guarantees ac:name present? The pattern matches `ac:name="(?:excerpt-include|table-excerpt-include)"` so yes.
5. `_includeMacroPattern` — matches `<ac:structured-macro ... ac:name="excerpt-include"...` — but the attribute order might differ: `ac:name` could come after other attributes; pattern `[^>]*ac:name="..."` requires ac:name after some attrs — fine since `[^>]*` matches zero. But what if ac:name comes with single quotes? Confluence always uses double quotes. OK.
6. Non-greedy `>.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` with dotAll — nested includes inside body: `.*?` stops at first closing tag. Nested structured-macro inside the body (like nested excerpt-include) would break matching — the outer match ends at the inner's close tag. Java regex probably the same. Parity concern but arguably acceptable.
7. `_attrOf` doesn't handle single-quoted attrs. Fine for parity.
8. `confluenceSpaceKeyOf`: `_expandable.space` link tail — splits by '/' and takes last. Real link like "/rest/api/space/DOCS" → "DOCS". OK. But v2 API uses `/wiki/api/v2/...`? fine.

Security: escaped mention re-embedded — good. But `_escapeMention` escapes `&` first — correct order.

Potential issue: mention resolution happens... order relative to excerpt inlining? In the pipeline, inliner first then mention resolver — mentions inside inlined excerpts get resolved. Fine.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

{"path":"lib/src/integrations/confluence/confluence_markdown_resolvers.dart"}

Note: `_escapeMention` escapes `&`, `<`, `>` but not quotes — that's fine for text. `_macroParamText` compares `_attrOf(open, 'ac:name') == paramName` — case sensitivity? Java Jsoup parameter() — probably exact. Hmm.

Potential issues to note:
1. `_findPage` cache stores null results too (good, caches misses). But cache is per inliner instance.
2. `_includeTarget`: `title!` — `_nonBlank(title) ? title : _macroParamText(...)`. If title from ri:content-title is blank and page-title param is used... fine. But there's a subtle bug: if the `ri:content-title` attribute is present but blank (e.g. `ri:content-title=""`), title falls to param. OK.
3. In `_resolveInclude`, `_storageValueOf(page)` is called before null check — page is `Map<String,dynamic>?`, `_storageValueOf` accepts nullable. Fine.
4. `_macroNameOf(macro)!` non-null asserted — the include macro pattern guarantees ac:name present? The pattern matches `ac:name="(?:excerpt-include|table-excerpt-include)"` so yes.
5. `_includeMacroPattern` — matches `<ac:structured-macro ... ac:name="excerpt-include"...` — but the attribute order might differ: `ac:name` could come after other attributes; pattern `[^>]*ac:name="..."` requires ac:name after some attrs — fine since `[^>]*` matches zero. But what if ac:name comes with single quotes? Confluence always uses double quotes. OK.
6. Non-greedy `>.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` with dotAll — nested includes inside body: `.*?` stops at first closing tag. Nested structured-macro inside the body (like nested excerpt-include) would break matching — the outer match ends at the inner's close tag. Java regex probably the same. Parity concern but arguably acceptable.
7. `_attrOf` doesn't handle single-quoted attrs. Fine for parity.
8. `confluenceSpaceKeyOf`: `_expandable.space` link tail — splits by '/' and takes last. Real link like "/rest/api/space/DOCS" → "DOCS". OK. But v2 API uses `/wiki/api/v2/...`? fine.

Now the mention resolver: it caches failed lookups per inliner instance. But the mention pattern requires `<ac:link...><ri:user...ri:account-id=...` — what about mentions where ri:user uses `ri:userkey` instead of account-id (older Confluence)? Java parity may handle only account-id; skip.

Security: escaped mention re-embedded — good. But `_escapeMention` escapes `&` first — correct order.

Potential issue: mention resolution happens... order relative to excerpt inlining? In the pipeline, inliner first then mention resolver — mentions inside inlined excerpts get resolved. Fine.

Now the storage file changes, sync downloader, sync_resolvers. Let me view the rest of the diff.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

Note: `_escapeMention` escapes `&`, `<`, `>` but not quotes — that's fine for text. `_macroParamText` compares `_attrOf(open, 'ac:name') == paramName` — case sensitivity? Java Jsoup parameter() — probably exact. Hmm.

Potential issues to note:
1. `_findPage` cache stores null results too (good, caches misses). But cache is per inliner instance.
2. `_includeTarget`: `title!` — `_nonBlank(title) ? title : _macroParamText(...)`. If title from ri:content-title is blank and page-title param is used... fine. But there's a subtle bug: if the `ri:content-title` attribute is present but blank (e.g. `ri:content-title=""`), title falls to param. OK.
3. In `_resolveInclude`, `_storageValueOf(page)` is called before null check — page is `Map<String,dynamic>?`, `_storageValueOf` accepts nullable. Fine.
4. `_macroNameOf(macro)!` non-null asserted — the include macro pattern guarantees ac:name present? The pattern matches `ac:name="(?:excerpt-include|table-excerpt-include)"` so yes.
5. `_includeMacroPattern` — matches `<ac:structured-macro ... ac:name="excerpt-include"...` — but the attribute order might differ: `ac:name` could come after other attributes; pattern `[^>]*ac:name="..."` requires ac:name after some attrs — fine since `[^>]*` matches zero. But what if ac:name comes with single quotes? Confluence always uses double quotes. OK.
6. Non-greedy `>.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` with dotAll — nested includes inside body: `.*?` stops at first closing tag. Nested structured-macro inside the body (like nested excerpt-include) would break matching — the outer match ends at the inner's close tag. Java regex probably the same. Parity concern but arguably acceptable.
7. `_attrOf` doesn't handle single-quoted attrs. Fine for parity.
8. `confluenceSpaceKeyOf`: `_expandable.space` link tail — splits by '/' and takes last. Real link like "/rest/api/space/DOCS" → "DOCS". OK. But v2 API uses `/wiki/api/v2/...`? fine.

Potential issue: mention resolution happens... order relative to excerpt inlining? In the pipeline, inliner first then mention resolver — mentions inside inlined excerpts get resolved. Fine.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

Note: `_escapeMention` escapes `&`, `<`, `>` but not quotes — that's fine for text. `_macroParamText` compares `_attrOf(open, 'ac:name') == paramName` — case sensitivity? Java Jsoup parameter() — probably exact. Hmm.

Potential issues to note:
1. `_findPage` cache stores null results too (good, caches misses). But cache is per inliner instance.
2. `_includeTarget`: `title!` — `_nonBlank(title) ? title : _macroParamText(...)`. If title from ri:content-title is blank and page-title param is used... fine. But there's a subtle bug: if the `ri:content-title` attribute is present but blank (e.g. `ri:content-title=""`), title falls to param. OK.
3. In `_resolveInclude`, `_storageValueOf(page)` is called before null check — page is `Map<String,dynamic>?`, `_storageValueOf` accepts nullable. Fine.
4. `_macroNameOf(macro)!` non-null asserted — the include macro pattern guarantees ac:name present? The pattern matches `ac:name="(?:excerpt-include|table-excerpt-include)"` so yes.
5. `_includeMacroPattern` — matches `<ac:structured-macro ... ac:name="excerpt-include"...` — but the attribute order might differ: `ac:name` could come after other attributes; pattern `[^>]*ac:name="..."` requires ac:name after some attrs — fine since `[^>]*` matches zero. But what if ac:name comes with single quotes? Confluence always uses double quotes. OK.
6. Non-greedy `>.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` with dotAll — nested includes inside body: `.*?` stops at first closing tag. Nested structured-macro inside the body (like nested excerpt-include) would break matching — the outer match ends at the inner's close tag. Java regex probably the same. Parity concern but arguably acceptable.
7. `_attrOf` doesn't handle single-quoted attrs. Fine for parity.
8. `confluenceSpaceKeyOf`: `_expandable.space` link tail — splits by '/' and takes last. Real link like "/rest/api/space/DOCS" → "DOCS". OK. But v2 API uses `/wiki/api/v2/...`? fine.

Security: escaped mention re-embedded — good. But `_escapeMention` escapes `&` first — correct order.

Potential issue: mention resolution happens... order relative to excerpt inlining? In the pipeline, inliner first then mention resolver — mentions inside inlined excerpts get resolved. Fine.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

2. `_includeTarget`: `title!` — `_nonBlank(title) ? title : _macroParamText(...)`. If title from ri:content-title is blank and page-title param is used... fine. But there's a subtle bug: if the `ri:content-title` attribute is present but blank (e.g. `ri:content-title=""`), title falls to param. OK.

But what if ac:name comes with single quotes? Confluence always uses double quotes. OK.
6. Non-greedy `>.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` with dotAll — nested includes inside body: `.*?` stops at first closing tag. Nested structured-macro inside the body (like nested excerpt-include) would break matching — the outer match ends at the inner's close tag. Java regex probably the same. Security: escaped mention re-embedded — good. But `_escapeMention` escapes `&` first — correct order.

Potential issue: mention resolution happens... order relative to excerpt inlining? In the pipeline, inliner first then mention resolver — mentions inside inlined excerpts get resolved. Fine.

Key review considerations:

1. **`_SyncConfluenceResolverClient.findContent` fallback bug**: In `_findPage`, space-specific search first, then default lookup. The Java parity. But caching: `_pageCache['SPACE|Target'] = page` — where page might have come from default lookup with spaceKey null. OK.

3. **Concurrency**: sync code, single-threaded. Fine.

4. **`_inlineNested` pattern overlap**: `_includeMacroPattern` matching nested macros — the non-greedy `.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` will end at the FIRST closing tag, so for a macro whose body contains another structured-macro, the outer match stops early, leaving trailing content of the outer macro unprocessed, and the remainder `</ac:structured-macro>` will be emitted as literal text. This could produce broken output for nested macros inside the include macro body. But include macros normally have only parameter bodies (ac:parameter), which contain ac:link not structured-macro. Java parity likely has same regex. Suggestion-level.

5. **`_attrOf` only handles double quotes** — parity with Java regex likely same. OK.

6. **`_firstTagInner` for `ac:rich-text-body`** — non-greedy to first close tag; nested rich-text-body unlikely.

7. **`_macroParamText` open tag extraction**: `m.group(0)!.substring(0, indexOf('>')+1)` — if parameter contains `>` inside attribute value... edge case, ignore.

8. **Case sensitivity of parameter name comparison**: `_attrOf(open, 'ac:name') == paramName` — exact case. Storage XML from Confluence uses exact names. Fine.

9. **`_wrapTimeTag` inserted before `_wrapAdfNode`** — order in `_wrapStorage`: fine.

But one subtlety: in `_tableToMarkdown`, cells use content? The test shows time inside table cells works.

11. **Mention pattern limitation**: mentions like `<ac:link ac:anchor="..."><ri:user .../></ac:link>` — pattern `<ac:link[^>]*>` fine.

But mentions where the ri:user tag has attributes in different order, e.g. `ri:account-id` before other attrs — pattern `<ri:user\b[^>]*?ri:account-id="..."` handles any order. Good.

What about `ri:user` with `ri:userkey` (legacy) — not handled; Java parity may also not. Skip.

12. **Security**: `userProfile` URL — accountId encoded. Good. Display name escaped. Good.

13. **`_whiteboardMarker`**: url param content inserted raw into markdown — `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): $url]` — if url contains `]` it could break markdown, but it's from Confluence storage; low risk.

14. **Two separate `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` instances** despite comment "reuse one HTTP-backed client" — cosmetic/doc mismatch; each resolver holds its own cache anyway. The inliner and mention resolver have separate caches regardless of shared client. Suggestion.

15. **Performance**: `_pageCache` never expires — per downloader instance, fine.

16. **`_findPage` behavior when space lookup returns a page without storage**: cached; ok.

18. In `_resolveInclude`, `visitKey` uses `page['id']` — if page has no id (echo fixture provides id; real API always has id), `'null|...'` — two different pages without ids would share cycle key... minor.

19. `inline()` early-return checks `contains('excerpt-include')` — also matches `table-excerpt-include` since it contains that substring. Good.

20. In `_includeTarget`, if the ri:page tag exists but has no title and no page-title param → null → macro kept. Good.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

Key review considerations:

1. **`_SyncConfluenceResolverClient.findContent` fallback bug**: In `_findPage`, space-specific search first, then default lookup. The Java parity. But caching: `_pageCache['SPACE|Target'] = page` — where page might have come from default lookup with spaceKey null. OK.

2. **Potential issue: `_findPage` caching negative results from the space-specific lookup then falling back to default** — actually if space lookup returns null, it does default lookup and caches the default result under the space key. Fine.

3. **Concurrency**: sync code, single-threaded. Fine.

4. **`_inlineNested` pattern overlap**: `_includeMacroPattern` matching nested macros — the non-greedy `.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` will end at the FIRST closing tag, so for a macro whose body contains another structured-macro, the outer match stops early, leaving trailing content of the outer macro unprocessed, and the remainder `</ac:structured-macro>` will be emitted as literal text. This could produce broken output for nested macros inside the include macro body. But include macros normally have only parameter bodies (ac:parameter), which contain ac:link not structured-macro. Java parity likely has same regex. Suggestion-level.

5. **`_attrOf` only handles double quotes** — parity with Java regex likely same. OK.

6. **`_firstTagInner` for `ac:rich-text-body`** — non-greedy to first close tag; nested rich-text-body unlikely.

7. **`_macroParamText` open tag extraction**: `m.group(0)!.substring(0, indexOf('>')+1)` — if parameter contains `>` inside attribute value... edge case, ignore.

8. **Case sensitivity of parameter name comparison**: `_attrOf(open, 'ac:name') == paramName` — exact case. Storage XML from Confluence uses exact names. Fine.

9. **`_wrapTimeTag` inserted before `_wrapAdfNode`** — order in `_wrapStorage`: fine.

10. **`_XmlNode.content` change with `time`**: `child.attrs['datetime'] ?? child.content`. What about `local-id`? fine. But wait — the `_childContent` for 'time' returns datetime only; what if time tag appears with body text and datetime? Java substitutes datetime. OK.

But one subtlety: in `_tableToMarkdown`, cells use content? The test shows time inside table cells works.

11. **Mention pattern limitation**: mentions like `<ac:link ac:anchor="..."><ri:user .../></ac:link>` — pattern `<ac:link[^>]*>` fine.

But mentions where the ri:user tag has attributes in different order, e.g. `ri:account-id` before other attrs — pattern `<ri:user\b[^>]*?ri:account-id="..."` handles any order. Good.

What about `ri:user` with `ri:userkey` (legacy) — not handled; Java parity may also not. Skip.

14. **Two separate `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` instances** despite comment "reuse one HTTP-backed client" — cosmetic/doc mismatch; each resolver holds its own cache anyway. The inliner and mention resolver have separate caches regardless of shared client. Suggestion.

15. **Performance**: `_pageCache` never expires — per downloader instance, fine.

16. **`_findPage` behavior when space lookup returns a page without storage**: cached; ok.

18. In `_resolveInclude`, `visitKey` uses `page['id']` — if page has no id (echo fixture provides id; real API always has id), `'null|...'` — two different pages without ids would share cycle key... minor.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

{"path":"lib/src/integrations/confluence/confluence_markdown_resolvers.dart"}

Note: `_escapeMention` escapes `&`, `<`, `>` but not quotes — that's fine for text. `_macroParamText` compares `_attrOf(open, 'ac:name') == paramName` — case sensitivity? Java Jsoup parameter() — probably exact. Hmm.

Potential issues to note:
1. `_findPage` cache stores null results too (good, caches misses). But cache is per inliner instance.
2. `_includeTarget`: `title!` — `_nonBlank(title) ? title : _macroParamText(...)`. If title from ri:content-title is blank and page-title param is used... fine. But there's a subtle bug: if the `ri:content-title` attribute is present but blank (e.g. `ri:content-title=""`), title falls to param. OK.
3. In `_resolveInclude`, `_storageValueOf(page)` is called before null check — page is `Map<String,dynamic>?`, `_storageValueOf` accepts nullable. Fine.
4. `_macroNameOf(macro)!` non-null asserted — the include macro pattern guarantees ac:name present? The pattern matches `ac:name="(?:excerpt-include|table-excerpt-include)"` so yes.
5. `_includeMacroPattern` — matches `<ac:structured-macro ... ac:name="excerpt-include"...` — but the attribute order might differ: `ac:name` could come after other attributes; pattern `[^>]*ac:name="..."` requires ac:name after some attrs — fine since `[^>]*` matches zero. But what if ac:name comes with single quotes? Confluence always uses double quotes. OK.
6. Non-greedy `>.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` with dotAll — nested includes inside body: `.*?` stops at first closing tag. Nested structured-macro inside the body (like nested excerpt-include) would break matching — the outer match ends at the inner's close tag. Java regex probably the same. Parity concern but arguably acceptable.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments.
