# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

2. `_includeTarget`: `title!` — `_nonBlank(title) ? title : _macroParamText(...)`. If title from ri:content-title is blank and page-title param is used... fine. But there's a subtle bug: if the `ri:content-title` attribute is present but blank (e.g. `ri:content-title=""`), title falls to param. OK.

But what if ac:name comes with single quotes? Confluence always uses double quotes. OK.
6. Non-greedy `>.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` with dotAll — nested includes inside body: `.*?` stops at first closing tag. Nested structured-macro inside the body (like nested excerpt-include) would break matching — the outer match ends at the inner's close tag. Java regex probably the same. - **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Deletions**: -7

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.

3. **Concurrency**: sync code, single-threaded. Fine.

4. **`_inlineNested` pattern overlap**: `_includeMacroPattern` matching nested macros — the non-greedy `.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` will end at the FIRST closing tag, so for a macro whose body contains another structured-macro, the outer match stops early, leaving trailing content of the outer macro unprocessed, and the remainder `</ac:structured-macro>` will be emitted as literal text. This could produce broken output for nested macros inside the include macro body. But include macros normally have only parameter bodies (ac:parameter), which contain ac:link not structured-macro. Java parity likely has same regex. Suggestion-level.

5. **`_attrOf` only handles double quotes** — parity with Java regex likely same. OK.

8. **Case sensitivity of parameter name comparison**: `_attrOf(open, 'ac:name') == paramName` — exact case. Storage XML from Confluence uses exact names. Fine.

9. **`_wrapTimeTag` inserted before `_wrapAdfNode`** — order in `_wrapStorage`: fine.

But mentions where the ri:user tag has attributes in different order, e.g. `ri:account-id` before other attrs — pattern `<ri:user\b[^>]*?ri:account-id="..."` handles any order. Good.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

3. **Concurrency**: sync code, single-threaded. Fine.

4. **`_inlineNested` pattern overlap**: `_includeMacroPattern` matching nested macros — the non-greedy `.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` will end at the FIRST closing tag, so for a macro whose body contains another structured-macro, the outer match stops early, leaving trailing content of the outer macro unprocessed, and the remainder `</ac:structured-macro>` will be emitted as literal text. This could produce broken output for nested macros inside the include macro body. But include macros normally have only parameter bodies (ac:parameter), which contain ac:link not structured-macro. Java parity likely has same regex. Suggestion-level.

5. **`_attrOf` only handles double quotes** — parity with Java regex likely same. OK.

6. **`_firstTagInner` for `ac:rich-text-body`** — non-greedy to first close tag; nested rich-text-body unlikely.

7. **`_macroParamText` open tag extraction**: `m.group(0)!.substring(0, indexOf('>')+1)` — if parameter contains `>` inside attribute value... edge case, ignore.

8. **Case sensitivity of parameter name comparison**: `_attrOf(open, 'ac:name') == paramName` — exact case. Storage XML from Confluence uses exact names. Fine.

9. **`_wrapTimeTag` inserted before `_wrapAdfNode`** — order in `_wrapStorage`: fine.

But one subtlety: in `_tableToMarkdown`, cells use content? The test shows time inside table cells works.

11. **Mention pattern limitation**: mentions like `<ac:link ac:anchor="..."><ri:user .../></ac:link>` — pattern `<ac:link[^>]*>` fine.

But mentions where the ri:user tag has attributes in different order, e.g. `ri:account-id` before other attrs — pattern `<ri:user\b[^>]*?ri:account-id="..."` handles any order. Good.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

3. **Concurrency**: sync code, single-threaded. Fine.

4. **`_inlineNested` pattern overlap**: `_includeMacroPattern` matching nested macros — the non-greedy `.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` will end at the FIRST closing tag, so for a macro whose body contains another structured-macro, the outer match stops early, leaving trailing content of the outer macro unprocessed, and the remainder `</ac:structured-macro>` will be emitted as literal text. This could produce broken output for nested macros inside the include macro body. But include macros normally have only parameter bodies (ac:parameter), which contain ac:link not structured-macro. Java parity likely has same regex. Suggestion-level.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

Potential issues to note:
1. `_findPage` cache stores null results too (good, caches misses). But cache is per inliner instance.
2. `_includeTarget`: `title!` — `_nonBlank(title) ? title : _macroParamText(...)`. If title from ri:content-title is blank and page-title param is used... fine. But there's a subtle bug: if the `ri:content-title` attribute is present but blank (e.g. `ri:content-title=""`), title falls to param. OK.
3. In `_resolveInclude`, `_storageValueOf(page)` is called before null check — page is `Map<String,dynamic>?`, `_storageValueOf` accepts nullable. Fine.
4. `_macroNameOf(macro)!` non-null asserted — the include macro pattern guarantees ac:name present? The pattern matches `ac:name="(?:excerpt-include|table-excerpt-include)"` so yes.
5. `_includeMacroPattern` — matches `<ac:structured-macro ... ac:name="excerpt-include"...` — but the attribute order might differ: `ac:name` could come after other attributes; pattern `[^>]*ac:name="..."` requires ac:name after some attrs — fine since `[^>]*` matches zero. But what if ac:name comes with single quotes? Confluence always uses double quotes. OK.
6. Non-greedy `>.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` with dotAll — nested includes inside body: `.*?` stops at first closing tag. Nested structured-macro inside the body (like nested excerpt-include) would break matching — the outer match ends at the inner's close tag. Java regex probably the same. Parity concern but arguably acceptable.

Potential issue: mention resolution happens... order relative to excerpt inlining? In the pipeline, inliner first then mention resolver — mentions inside inlined excerpts get resolved. Fine.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |

| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 362
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/362
- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-347` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +953
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:50:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:02:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```

Full suite: 3662 tests passed, 16 skipped (coverage 96.7%).

<details>
<summary>Pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PAGE[page storage HTML] --> SK[confluenceSpaceKeyOf]
  SK --> INL[ConfluenceExcerptInliner]
  INL -->|findContent title+space, cache, depth<=3, cycle set| INL
  INL --> MEN[ConfluenceMentionResolver]
  MEN -->|user?accountId -> displayName, cache| MEN
  MEN --> MD[confluenceStorageToMarkdown]
  MD --> FILE[page.md]
```

</details>

4. **`_inlineNested` pattern overlap**: `_includeMacroPattern` matching nested macros — the non-greedy `.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` will end at the FIRST closing tag, so for a macro whose body contains another structured-macro, the outer match stops early, leaving trailing content of the outer macro unprocessed, and the remainder `</ac:structured-macro>` will be emitted as literal text. This could produce broken output for nested macros inside the include macro body. But include macros normally have only parameter bodies (ac:parameter), which contain ac:link not structured-macro. # AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

💡 **SUGGESTION: include-macro regex truncates on nested structured-macro bodies**

The body alternative `>.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*?>` is non-greedy, so `_includeMacroPattern` ends at the **first** closing `</ac:structured-macro>` it sees. If an `excerpt-include` macro's own body ever nests another `ac:structured-macro` (e.g. a macro inside a `page-title`/`name` parameter value), the match stops mid-body and the leftover `</ac:structured-macro>` is emitted as literal text into the converted Markdown.

Confluence never generates such nesting for include macros, and the Java original shares the same regex shape, so this is parity-faithful — but a one-line comment on the pattern (like the one `_rawMacrosOfKind` has for its depth-aware scan) plus a regression test pinning "macro left verbatim / no dangling close tag" would lock the assumption and document why the depth-aware scan wasn't reused here.

💡 **SUGGESTION: cycle-protection key collapses when the page has no `id`**

```dart
final visitKey = '${page['id']}|${_normalizeExcerptName(name)}|$kind';
```

If a resolved page carries no `id` key (a minimal/mocked API response, or a proxy that strips fields), `page['id']` stringifies to the literal `null`, so two *different* id-less target pages with the same excerpt name/kind would produce the same key and the second one would be misclassified as a cycle (`path.add` returns false → include left verbatim).

Real Confluence v1 responses always include `id`, so this is cosmetic in practice. Using `page['id'] ?? title` or `?? cacheKey` would make the guard robust for id-less payloads at zero cost.

💡 **SUGGESTION: doc/impl mismatch — two resolver clients are created, not one**

The constructor doc says "the excerpt-include inliner and mention resolver reuse one HTTP-backed client", but the initializer list constructs **two** separate `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` instances:

```dart
_excerptInliner = ConfluenceExcerptInliner(_SyncConfluenceResolverClient(_config)),
_mentionResolver = ConfluenceMentionResolver(_SyncConfluenceResolverClient(_config)),
```

Functionally this is harmless (the clients are stateless; the inliner and resolver keep their own caches regardless), but either build a single `final client = _SyncConfluenceResolverClient(_config);` and share it — matching the doc and the Java `ConfluencePageDownloader` shape — or reword the doc to "each gets an HTTP-backed client". Sharing one instance would also make the intent explicit if `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` ever gains state (e.g. a shared HTTP connection pool).

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: include-macro regex truncates on nested structured-macro bodies**

The body alternative `>.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*?>` is non-greedy, so `_includeMacroPattern` ends at the **first** closing `</ac:structured-macro>` it sees. If an `excerpt-include` macro's own body ever nests another `ac:structured-macro` (e.g. a macro inside a `page-title`/`name` parameter value), the match stops mid-body and the leftover `</ac:structured-macro>` is emitted as literal text into the converted Markdown.

Confluence never generates such nesting for include macros, and the Java original shares the same regex shape, so this is parity-faithful — but a one-line comment on the pattern (like the one `_rawMacrosOfKind` has for its depth-aware scan) plus a regression test pinning "macro left verbatim / no dangling close tag" would lock the assumption and document why the depth-aware scan wasn't reused here.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: cycle-protection key collapses when the page has no `id`**

```dart
final visitKey = '${page['id']}|${_normalizeExcerptName(name)}|$kind';
```

If a resolved page carries no `id` key (a minimal/mocked API response, or a proxy that strips fields), `page['id']` stringifies to the literal `null`, so two *different* id-less target pages with the same excerpt name/kind would produce the same key and the second one would be misclassified as a cycle (`path.add` returns false → include left verbatim).

Real Confluence v1 responses always include `id`, so this is cosmetic in practice. Using `page['id'] ?? title` or `?? cacheKey` would make the guard robust for id-less payloads at zero cost.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: doc/impl mismatch — two resolver clients are created, not one**

The constructor doc says "the excerpt-include inliner and mention resolver reuse one HTTP-backed client", but the initializer list constructs **two** separate `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` instances:

```dart
_excerptInliner = ConfluenceExcerptInliner(_SyncConfluenceResolverClient(_config)),
_mentionResolver = ConfluenceMentionResolver(_SyncConfluenceResolverClient(_config)),
```

Functionally this is harmless (the clients are stateless; the inliner and resolver keep their own caches regardless), but either build a single `final client = _SyncConfluenceResolverClient(_config);` and share it — matching the doc and the Java `ConfluencePageDownloader` shape — or reword the doc to "each gets an HTTP-backed client". Sharing one instance would also make the intent explicit if `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` ever gains state (e.g. a shared HTTP connection pool).
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

- **Title**: gh-347 parity: Confluence conversion fixes (excerpt includes, space links, whiteboard, placeholders, mentions/dates, synced blocks)

## PR Description

Closes #347
## What changed

Ported the Java Confluence conversion-fix batch (dm.ai `932e0db0`, `0b658b70`, `bb1b51e9`; synced blocks `1ec63e18` were already ported) to the Dart converter and sync downloader:

- **Excerpt includes** — new `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` (Java `ConfluenceExcerptInliner` 1:1): materializes `excerpt-include` / `table-excerpt-include` macros from the target page's storage, with space-less `ri:page` links resolved in the containing page's space, name normalization (case/whitespace/` `), blank-name → unnamed-else-all semantics, depth-3 nesting with cycle protection, page caching, and unresolved macros left verbatim. Wired into `_PageDownloader` ahead of Markdown conversion.
- **User mentions + dates** — new `ConfluenceMentionResolver` replaces `<ac:link><ri:user…></ac:link>` with `@Display Name` (cached, XML-escaped, unresolvable left untouched); `<time datetime="…">` lozenges now render their date (including inside table cells).
- **Whiteboard marker** — `native-embed:whiteboard` macros render `[Whiteboard (content not available via API): url]` instead of an empty code fence.
- **Placeholder regressions locked** — the Dart converter parses storage XML directly (no placeholder stash), so the `0b658b70` prefix-collision class of bugs cannot occur; parity tests pin 13-table and code-in-table-cell behavior.
- **`Content.getSpaceKey` parity** — `confluenceSpaceKeyOf` reads `space.key` or the `_expandable.space` link tail; used for the page-space resolution above.

### Key decisions

- Resolvers live in `confluence_markdown.dart` as a part file and depend on an injectable `ConfluenceResolverClient` (mirrors the existing `ConfluencePageOperations`/`SyncAttachmentHelper` collaborator pattern), so the Java Mockito-based tests port 1:1 without HTTP; the sync bridge injects `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` (REST via `SyncHttpClient`).
- The Java downloader's internal-`ac:link` graph walking has no Dart counterpart (documented limitation: link-graph walking is limited to child pages), so its "space-less links in page space" behavior is covered only where it exists in Dart — the excerpt inliner.
- End-to-end coverage: echo-server fixtures (page 888 + `Source` + `user?accountId`) drive `confluence_download_pages` through excerpt inlining + mention resolution; Java `ConfluenceHtmlToMarkdownTest` cases ported to `confluence_markdown_test.dart`.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/ test/js/sync_tools/confluence_java_name_tools_test.dart
dart analyze && crap4dart check --all && crap4dart analyze   # 20 gates pass, Max CRAP 8.00
```


Key review considerations:

2. **Potential issue: `_findPage` caching negative results from the space-specific lookup then falling back to default** — actually if space lookup returns null, it does default lookup and caches the default result under the space key. Fine.

3. **Concurrency**: sync code, single-threaded. Fine.

4. **`_inlineNested` pattern overlap**: `_includeMacroPattern` matching nested macros — the non-greedy `.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*>` will end at the FIRST closing tag, so for a macro whose body contains another structured-macro, the outer match stops early, leaving trailing content of the outer macro unprocessed, and the remainder `</ac:structured-macro>` will be emitted as literal text. This could produce broken output for nested macros inside the include macro body. But include macros normally have only parameter bodies (ac:parameter), which contain ac:link not structured-macro. Java parity likely has same regex. Suggestion-level.

5. **`_attrOf` only handles double quotes** — parity with Java regex likely same. OK.

6. **`_firstTagInner` for `ac:rich-text-body`** — non-greedy to first close tag; nested rich-text-body unlikely.

7. **`_macroParamText` open tag extraction**: `m.group(0)!.substring(0, indexOf('>')+1)` — if parameter contains `>` inside attribute value... edge case, ignore.

8. **Case sensitivity of parameter name comparison**: `_attrOf(open, 'ac:name') == paramName` — exact case. Storage XML from Confluence uses exact names. Fine.

9. **`_wrapTimeTag` inserted before `_wrapAdfNode`** — order in `_wrapStorage`: fine.

10. **`_XmlNode.content` change with `time`**: `child.attrs['datetime'] ?? child.content`. What about `local-id`? fine. But wait — the `_childContent` for 'time' returns datetime only; what if time tag appears with body text and datetime? Java substitutes datetime. OK.

But one subtlety: in `_tableToMarkdown`, cells use content? The test shows time inside table cells works.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |

| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: include-macro regex truncates on nested structured-macro bodies**

The body alternative `>.*?</ac:structured-macro\s*?>` is non-greedy, so `_includeMacroPattern` ends at the **first** closing `</ac:structured-macro>` it sees. If an `excerpt-include` macro's own body ever nests another `ac:structured-macro` (e.g. a macro inside a `page-title`/`name` parameter value), the match stops mid-body and the leftover `</ac:structured-macro>` is emitted as literal text into the converted Markdown.

Confluence never generates such nesting for include macros, and the Java original shares the same regex shape, so this is parity-faithful — but a one-line comment on the pattern (like the one `_rawMacrosOfKind` has for its depth-aware scan) plus a regression test pinning "macro left verbatim / no dangling close tag" would lock the assumption and document why the depth-aware scan wasn't reused here.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: cycle-protection key collapses when the page has no `id`**

```dart
final visitKey = '${page['id']}|${_normalizeExcerptName(name)}|$kind';
```

If a resolved page carries no `id` key (a minimal/mocked API response, or a proxy that strips fields), `page['id']` stringifies to the literal `null`, so two *different* id-less target pages with the same excerpt name/kind would produce the same key and the second one would be misclassified as a cycle (`path.add` returns false → include left verbatim).

Real Confluence v1 responses always include `id`, so this is cosmetic in practice. Using `page['id'] ?? title` or `?? cacheKey` would make the guard robust for id-less payloads at zero cost.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: doc/impl mismatch — two resolver clients are created, not one**

The constructor doc says "the excerpt-include inliner and mention resolver reuse one HTTP-backed client", but the initializer list constructs **two** separate `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` instances:

```dart
_excerptInliner = ConfluenceExcerptInliner(_SyncConfluenceResolverClient(_config)),
_mentionResolver = ConfluenceMentionResolver(_SyncConfluenceResolverClient(_config)),
```

Functionally this is harmless (the clients are stateless; the inliner and resolver keep their own caches regardless), but either build a single `final client = _SyncConfluenceResolverClient(_config);` and share it — matching the doc and the Java `ConfluencePageDownloader` shape — or reword the doc to "each gets an HTTP-backed client". Sharing one instance would also make the intent explicit if `_SyncConfluenceResolverClient` ever gains state (e.g. a shared HTTP connection pool).
